knowledge:
- key_parameters: scExp=A SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell gene counts and cell-level metadata ;; subjectVar=Character string specifying the metadata column in scExp that identifies the subject or biological sample (e.g., "orig.ident") ;; cellVar=Character string specifying the metadata column in scExp that identifies the cell type (e.g., "celltype")
- alternatives: Cell-level differential expression analysis (e.g., using Seurat's FindMarkers() or running DESeq2 directly on individual cells), which does not account for biological replication and can inflate false positives.
- when_to_use: When analyzing scRNA-seq data collected from multiple subjects (biological replicates or technical replicates) and wanting to perform differential gene expression analysis between populations (e.g., healthy vs. diseased) while properly accounting for subject-level variation (pseudo-bulk approach).
- pitfalls: Running cell-level differential expression analysis without aggregation, which treats cells as independent observations and ignores the correlation of cells within the same subject (leading to inflated false discovery rates) ;; If multiple assays are present in the input SingleCellExperiment object, only the first assay slot is used by default ;; Ensure the metadata variable for cell type is coerced or formatted correctly (the function will output a warning/message: "Coercing metadata variable to character").

workflows.name: pseudobulk_aggregation_and_dge
workflows.intent: Aggregate single-cell RNA-seq counts by subject and cell type to perform subject-level pseudo-bulk differential gene expression analysis.
input: small_airway (SingleCellExperiment object containing single-cell count matrix and cell-level metadata including subject and cell type annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Aggregate gene counts within subjects using countsBySubject() ;; 2. Summarize metadata to retain inter-subject variation using subjectMetaData() ;; 3. Combine aggregation and metadata summarization into a SummarizedExperiment using summarizedCounts() ;; 4. Stratify and aggregate counts across all cell types using aggregateBioVar() ;; 5. Perform downstream differential gene expression analysis on a specific cell type using DESeq2 (via DESeqDataSetFromMatrix() and DESeq())
workflows.code:
countsBySubject(scExp = small_airway, subjectVar = "orig.ident")
subjectMetaData(scExp = small_airway, subjectVar = "orig.ident")
summarizedCounts(scExp = small_airway, subjectVar = "orig.ident")
aggregateBioVar(scExp = small_airway,
                subjectVar = "orig.ident", cellVar = "celltype")
aggregate_counts <-
    aggregateBioVar(
        scExp = small_airway,
        subjectVar = "orig.ident", cellVar = "celltype"
    )
subj_dds_dataset <-
    DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
        countData = assay(aggregate_counts$`Secretory cell`, "counts"),
        colData = colData(aggregate_counts$`Secretory cell`),
        design = ~ Genotype
    )

subj_dds <- DESeq(subj_dds_dataset)

subj_dds_results <-
    results(subj_dds, contrast = c("Genotype", "WT", "CFTRKO"))
